meta.threshold: Every Commonwealth grant award must be published on GrantConnect within 21 days of the agreement taking effect (mandatory since 31 December 2017). Aggregate awards bundle many small recipients and are shown as not disclosed.
caveats: Grant totals are awarded values as published; a varied award counts at its current value. Aggregate awards and awards whose recipient was withheld sit in the not-disclosed bucket.
A recipient counts as a donor when its ABN, or a unique organisation name, matches an entity in the donor register (AEC returns and the exposed state registers). People are never matched by name.
AEC donations and state-register gifts are shown side by side and never summed: AEC returns already include state branch receipts.
A donor receiving a grant is a fact about the public record, not a finding: most programs are open and competitive, and the selection process is shown wherever the source records it.

Recipient ABNs, locations and selection processes come from each award's detail page; the share of dollars with a detail page fetched is in counts.electorate_known_share and counts.abn_known_share. Electorates are mapped from the delivery or recipient postcode and are approximate where a postcode straddles a boundary or a redistribution moved it.

grants.n: Spring Street Creek Naturalisation and Wetlands Project

The project will undertake Stage 1 of the UMA Youth and Community Centre expansion. Stage 1 includes earthworks and site preparation, construction of an underground carpark and construction of the central office building (building 5).
Construction of a 5 storey car park at the existing Edgebaston Road car park to create 200 car spaces
The grant activity is the construction of the Bill Delauney Reserve Amenities building
Facility and building refurbishment, including field revitalisation of Riverine Park
The Activity is Stage 1, which will prepare the site for establishment of a community centre.
The redevelopment of the Max Parker Pool (Stage 1) project will undertake the planning and design for the future upgrade of the Max Parker Pool
The project will construct a sporting field including installation of an automatic irrigation system, sub-surface drainage and natural sports turf at Peakhurst Park.
Install six 15m light poles around the perimeter, each with two new luminaires, install conduit and cables for the perimeter lighting, and upgrade the luminaires on the 8m poles at the lower field.
The project will upgrade a building in Revesby to establish an emergency crisis shelter for women and children escaping homelessness and domestic and family violence.

The CCTV Cameras at Chivers Hill Shops Lugarno project will install CCTV cameras in the Chivers Hill shopping precinct of Lugarno. This will include four outdoor cameras, mounting equipment, data support and installation.
